bobkit_architect_best_practices.overview: Best practices and guidelines for the BobKit-Architect mode to ensure high-quality planning artifacts, clear dependencies, and smooth transitions to implementation.

principle.name: Constitution First
principle.description: Always validate against project constitution before proceeding. Constitution violations are non-negotiable and must be resolved.
principle.rationale: The constitution defines the project's core principles and constraints. Ignoring or diluting these principles leads to technical debt and architectural drift.
principle.application: - Load constitution at start of every planning phase - Check each design decision against constitutional principles - Flag violations as CRITICAL in analysis - Never proceed with implementation if constitution conflicts exist

principle.name: Progressive Disclosure
principle.description: Load and process only the information needed for the current step. Avoid dumping entire files into context.
principle.rationale: Token efficiency is critical for complex planning tasks. Loading unnecessary context wastes tokens and reduces analysis quality.
principle.application: - Extract specific sections from specs and plans - Summarize long sections into key points - Use targeted queries instead of full file reads - Load additional context only when gaps detected

principle.name: Traceability Throughout
principle.description: Maintain clear traceability from requirements through tasks. Every task should map to requirements, every requirement should have tasks.
principle.rationale: Traceability ensures completeness, enables impact analysis, and facilitates validation. Missing traceability leads to scope creep and missed requirements.
principle.application: - Map tasks to user stories and requirements - Reference spec sections in plan decisions - Include requirement IDs in task descriptions - Generate coverage reports in analysis phase

principle.name: Dependency Clarity
principle.description: Make all dependencies explicit. Tasks should have clear prerequisites and blocking relationships.
principle.rationale: Clear dependencies enable parallel execution, prevent rework, and ensure correct implementation order.
principle.application: - Order tasks by dependency (foundational first) - Mark parallelizable tasks with [P] - Create dependency graphs showing completion order - Validate no circular dependencies exist

principle.name: Actionable Artifacts
principle.description: Every artifact should be immediately actionable without additional context. Tasks should be specific enough for direct implementation.
principle.rationale: Vague or incomplete artifacts require clarification loops, slowing development and increasing risk of misinterpretation.
principle.application: - Include exact file paths in tasks - Specify concrete acceptance criteria - Provide clear success metrics - Avoid ambiguous terms without definitions

practice.name: Script Execution First
practice.rule: Always run setup scripts before any planning work
practice.rationale: Scripts provide canonical paths and ensure consistent environment
practice.example: Run setup-plan.sh or check-prerequisites.sh to get FEATURE_DIR, BRANCH_NAME, and other required paths before loading any files.

practice.name: Resolve All Clarifications
practice.rule: Phase 0 must resolve ALL "NEEDS CLARIFICATION" markers
practice.rationale: Unresolved clarifications block design and lead to rework
practice.approach: - Extract all NEEDS CLARIFICATION from Technical Context - Generate research tasks for each unknown - Consolidate findings in research.md with Decision/Rationale/Alternatives - Update plan with resolved information

practice.name: Data Model First
practice.rule: Define data entities before API contracts
practice.rationale: APIs operate on data; data model drives contract design
practice.approach: - Extract entities from functional requirements - Define fields, relationships, validation rules - Document state transitions if applicable - Use data model to inform contract generation

practice.name: Constitution Check Twice
practice.rule: Validate against constitution before AND after design
practice.rationale: Design decisions may introduce new constitutional conflicts
practice.checkpoints: - Initial check: Validate spec against constitution - Post-design check: Validate plan, data model, contracts against constitution - Flag any violations as blocking issues

practice.name: Update Agent Context
practice.rule: Run agent context update scripts after Phase 1 design
practice.rationale: Keeps AI assistants informed of new technologies and patterns
practice.approach: - Run update-agent-context script with appropriate agent type - Script detects which AI agent is in use - Updates agent-specific context file - Preserves manual additions between markers

practice.name: User Story Organization
practice.rule: Organize tasks by user story, not by technical layer
practice.rationale: Enables independent implementation and testing of complete features
practice.structure: - Phase 1: Setup (project initialization) - Phase 2: Foundational (blocking prerequisites) - Phase 3+: One phase per user story (priority order) - Final Phase: Polish and cross-cutting concerns
practice.example: Instead of "Phase: Models" with all models, create "Phase: User Story 1" with models, services, and endpoints needed for that story.

practice.name: Strict Checklist Format
practice.rule: Every task MUST follow: - [ ] [TaskID] [P?] [Story?] Description with file path
practice.rationale: Consistent format enables parsing, tracking, and automation
practice.components: - Checkbox: Always - [ ] - Task ID: Sequential T001, T002, T003... - [P] marker: Only for parallelizable tasks - [Story] label: US1, US2, etc. for user story phases only - Description: Clear action with exact file path

examples.good: - [ ] T001 Create project structure per implementation plan
- [ ] T005 [P] Implement authentication middleware in src/middleware/auth.py
- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Create User model in src/models/user.py
examples.bad: - [ ] Create User model (missing ID and file path)

practice.name: Dependency Graph Generation
practice.rule: Always generate dependency graph showing user story completion order
practice.rationale: Visualizes critical path and enables parallel execution planning
practice.content: - Show which stories can be implemented in parallel - Identify blocking dependencies between stories - Highlight foundational tasks that block multiple stories - Provide parallel execution examples per story

practice.name: Task Completeness Validation
practice.rule: Validate each user story has all needed tasks and is independently testable
practice.rationale: Incomplete task lists lead to implementation gaps and rework
practice.checklist: - Each story has models, services, endpoints, integration tasks - Each story has independent test criteria - Each story can be completed without waiting for other stories - File paths are specific and unambiguous

practice.name: Tests Are Optional
practice.rule: Only generate test tasks if explicitly requested in spec or by user
practice.rationale: Not all projects require TDD; avoid imposing unnecessary overhead
practice.approach: - Check spec for testing requirements - Check user input for TDD preference - If tests requested: Include test tasks before implementation in each story phase - If not requested: Focus on implementation tasks only

practice.name: Unit Tests for Requirements
practice.rule: Checklists test requirement QUALITY, not implementation correctness
practice.rationale: Checklists validate that requirements are well-written, not that code works
practice.focus: - Completeness: Are all necessary requirements present? - Clarity: Are requirements unambiguous and specific? - Consistency: Do requirements align without conflicts? - Measurability: Can requirements be objectively verified? - Coverage: Are all scenarios/edge cases addressed?
practice.prohibited: - ❌ "Verify the button clicks correctly" - ❌ "Test error handling works" - ❌ "Confirm API returns 200"
practice.required: - ✅ "Are visual hierarchy requirements defined for all card types?" - ✅ "Is 'prominent display' quantified with specific sizing/positioning?" - ✅ "Are hover state requirements consistent across all interactive elements?"

practice.name: Dynamic Clarification Questions
practice.rule: Generate contextual questions from user input, not pre-baked catalog
practice.rationale: Generic questions waste time; targeted questions improve checklist quality
practice.approach: - Extract signals from user phrasing and spec/plan/tasks - Generate max 3 initial questions - Skip questions if already unambiguous in user input - May ask up to 2 more follow-ups if scenario classes unclear (max 5 total) - Focus on scope, risk, depth, audience, boundaries

practice.name: Minimum 80% Traceability
practice.rule: At least 80% of checklist items must include traceability references
practice.rationale: Traceability enables validation and ensures checklist covers actual requirements
practice.references: - Spec section: [Spec §X.Y] - Gap marker: [Gap] - Ambiguity marker: [Ambiguity] - Conflict marker: [Conflict] - Assumption marker: [Assumption]

practice.name: Content Consolidation
practice.rule: Soft cap at 40 items; prioritize by risk/impact
practice.rationale: Too many items reduce focus; consolidation improves usability
practice.approach: - Merge near-duplicates checking same requirement aspect - If >5 low-impact edge cases, create one consolidated item - Prioritize high-risk areas (security, data integrity, UX) - Focus on actionable findings over exhaustive coverage

practice.name: Descriptive Filenames
practice.rule: Use short, descriptive names based on domain (ux.md, api.md, security.md)
practice.rationale: Clear names enable easy identification and navigation
practice.approach: - Each run creates NEW file (never overwrites) - Use domain-specific names that indicate checklist purpose - Avoid generic names like "checklist1.md" - Clean up obsolete checklists when done

practice.name: Strictly Read-Only
practice.rule: NEVER modify files during analysis; only output reports
practice.rationale: Analysis should be non-destructive; modifications require user approval
practice.approach: - Load artifacts for analysis only - Generate findings and recommendations - Offer remediation plan (user must approve) - If user approves, use separate commands to apply fixes

practice.name: High-Signal Findings Only
practice.rule: Limit to 50 findings; aggregate remainder in overflow summary
practice.rationale: Too many findings reduce actionability; focus on high-impact issues
practice.priorities: - CRITICAL: Constitution violations, missing core artifacts, zero coverage - HIGH: Duplicates, conflicts, ambiguous security/performance - MEDIUM: Terminology drift, missing non-functional coverage - LOW: Style/wording improvements, minor redundancy

practice.name: Coverage Mapping
practice.rule: Map every requirement to tasks; identify gaps and orphans
practice.rationale: Ensures completeness and prevents scope gaps
practice.outputs: - Coverage summary table (requirement → tasks) - Unmapped tasks (tasks with no requirement) - Coverage percentage (requirements with ≥1 task) - Gap analysis (requirements with zero tasks)

practice.name: Constitution Authority
practice.rule: Constitution conflicts are automatically CRITICAL
practice.rationale: Constitution defines non-negotiable principles; violations must be fixed
practice.approach: - Load constitution principles and normative statements - Check each requirement and design decision against principles - Flag any MUST violations as CRITICAL - Require adjustment of spec/plan/tasks, not constitution dilution

practice.name: Actionable Next Steps
practice.rule: Always provide concrete next actions based on findings
practice.rationale: Analysis without action guidance is incomplete
practice.content: - If CRITICAL: Recommend resolving before implementation - If LOW/MEDIUM: User may proceed with improvement suggestions - Provide explicit command suggestions (e.g., "Run /bobkit.specify with refinement") - Offer remediation plan for top N issues

practice.name: Validate Before Transition
practice.rule: Ensure all prerequisites met before transitioning to next mode
practice.rationale: Premature transitions lead to rework and incomplete artifacts
practice.checkpoints: - Plan complete: All NEEDS CLARIFICATION resolved, constitution validated - Tasks complete: All user stories have tasks, dependencies clear - Analysis complete: No CRITICAL issues, coverage acceptable

practice.name: Clear Transition Signals
practice.rule: Explicitly state when ready to transition and why
practice.rationale: Clear signals help users understand workflow progress
practice.format: - State current phase completion - List artifacts generated - Indicate readiness for next phase - Suggest next command - Explain transition reason

practice.name: Preserve Context Across Transitions
practice.rule: Ensure all necessary context is captured in artifacts before transition
practice.rationale: Context loss leads to rework and inconsistencies
practice.approach: - Document all decisions in plan/tasks - Include rationale for key choices - Reference constitution principles used - Maintain traceability to requirements

pitfall.name: Ignoring Constitution
pitfall.description: Proceeding with design that violates constitutional principles
pitfall.why_problematic: Creates technical debt and architectural drift
pitfall.correct_approach: Always validate against constitution; flag violations as CRITICAL

pitfall.name: Vague Task Descriptions
pitfall.description: Tasks without specific file paths or clear acceptance criteria
pitfall.why_problematic: Leads to implementation ambiguity and rework
pitfall.correct_approach: Include exact file paths and specific, measurable outcomes

pitfall.name: Missing Dependencies
pitfall.description: Tasks without clear prerequisites or blocking relationships
pitfall.why_problematic: Causes implementation order errors and rework
pitfall.correct_approach: Create dependency graph; order tasks by prerequisites

pitfall.name: Implementation Testing Checklists
pitfall.description: Checklist items that test code behavior instead of requirement quality
pitfall.why_problematic: Confuses requirements validation with implementation testing
pitfall.correct_approach: Focus on requirement completeness, clarity, consistency, not code correctness

pitfall.name: Incomplete Coverage Analysis
pitfall.description: Not mapping all requirements to tasks or identifying orphaned tasks
pitfall.why_problematic: Leads to scope gaps and wasted implementation effort
pitfall.correct_approach: Generate coverage tables; identify gaps and orphans

pitfall.name: Token Waste
pitfall.description: Loading entire files into context when only sections needed
pitfall.why_problematic: Reduces analysis quality and increases costs
pitfall.correct_approach: Use progressive disclosure; load only necessary sections
